## 🎼 General Overview

- **Title**: Canon in D  
- **Composer**: Johann Pachelbel  
- **Arranger**: lemontart  
- **Tempo**: ♩ = 100 (quarter note = 100 BPM)  
- **Key Signature**: **D major** — two sharps: F♯ and C♯  
- **Time Signature**: **4/4** (common time) — four quarter notes per measure  
- **Instrumentation**: Piano (treble and bass clef)  
- **Dynamic Markings**:  
  - *p* (piano) at start of first system → soft  
  - *m* (mezzo) at start of second system → moderately loud (though unusual placement; typically “mf” or “mp”)  

---

## 🎵 Clefs & Note Ranges

### Treble Clef (Right Hand)
- Used for melody/harmony in higher register.
- In measures 1–4: **rests only** (whole rests).

### Bass Clef (Left Hand)
- Provides arpeggiated accompaniment throughout.
- All measures contain **eighth-note arpeggios** spanning two octaves, following the chord progression of the Canon.

---

## 🔑 Key Signature: D Major
- Sharps: **F♯, C♯**
- Applies to all F and C notes unless canceled by accidentals (none here).

## ⏱️ Time Signature: 4/4
- Each measure contains 4 quarter-note beats.
- Eighth notes = half a beat each.

---

## 📜 Measure-by-Measure Breakdown

> Note: All bass clef patterns are **arpeggiated eighth notes**, repeating every measure with slight variation based on harmony.

---

- The arrangement simplifies the original Canon into a repeating 4-measure loop with a descending melody starting in measure 5.
